back: A method that integrates the scope, schedule and cost baselines and compares them with actual performance, all expressed in money.
The scope, schedule and cost baselines integrated. Earned value is measured against it.
The authorized budget assigned to the scheduled work. How much work should be done by now. Excludes management reserve.
The measure of work performed, expressed as the budget authorized for that work. How much work is actually done.
The realized cost incurred for the work performed. How much the completed work actually cost.
The sum of all budgets established for the work to be performed. The total planned value.
EV = percent complete × BAC.
CV = EV − AC. Negative = over budget. Positive = under budget.
SV = EV − PV. Negative = behind schedule. Positive = ahead of schedule.
CPI = EV ÷ AC. Below 1.0 = over budget. Above 1.0 = under budget.
SPI = EV ÷ PV. Below 1.0 = behind schedule. Above 1.0 = ahead of schedule.

front: What comes first in CV, SV, CPI and SPI?
back: EV, always. Cost formulas then use AC; schedule formulas use PV.
For every $1 spent, the project gets 80 cents of work. Over budget.
The project is progressing at 120% of the planned rate. Ahead of schedule.
The expected total cost of completing all the work.

front: EAC if current cost performance continues
back: EAC = BAC ÷ CPI. The most common formula.

front: EAC if the variance was a one-time event
back: EAC = AC + (BAC − EV). Remaining work is done at the planned rate.

front: EAC if the original plan is no longer valid
back: EAC = AC + bottom-up ETC. The remaining work is re-estimated.

front: EAC if both cost and schedule affect the remaining work
back: EAC = AC + (BAC − EV) ÷ (CPI × SPI).
The expected cost to finish the remaining work. ETC = EAC − AC.
VAC = BAC − EAC. Negative = expected to finish over budget.
The cost efficiency needed on the remaining work to meet a goal. TCPI = (BAC − EV) ÷ (BAC − AC): work remaining ÷ funds remaining.
Harder to complete within the goal: the remaining work must be done more efficiently than planned. Below 1.0 = easier.
No earned value until the work is finished, then 100%. For short work within one reporting period.
50% of the value is earned when the work starts and 50% when it finishes. For work spanning two or three reporting periods.
A set share of the value is earned as each objective, verifiable milestone is reached.
Work that cannot be measured, such as project management. Value is earned with the passage of time. Keep to a minimum.
Supporting work, such as inspection and testing, whose earned value is a set proportion of the work it supports.

front: Schedule variance at the end of a project
back: Always zero, because all planned work has been earned (EV = PV = BAC), even if the project finished late.
PV = story points planned for the iteration. EV = story points of the stories actually done. AC = cost of the team for the iteration.
